name: Film grain revival
summary: Photographs with visible grain, soft halation and warm colour, made on 35mm film or graded to look like it. The look says that a real moment passed through a real roll.

philosophy.core_thesis: Grain and imperfection give a picture a body, so the viewer believes it was lived and not rendered.
design_principles: Shoot on 35mm colour negative film at ISO 400, such as Portra 400, Gold 200 or Ektar 100, and scan at 4000 dpi.
Use a 35mm or 50mm prime at f/2 to f/4, with a shutter of 1/125s or faster.
Expose 1 stop over for the negative; let highlights roll off with a soft shoulder.
Add halation around highlights by a red glow of 3 to 10px at 20% amount.
Allow light leaks, dust and an uneven frame edge in no more than 10% of frames.
Keep the grade warm at 5200–5600K with lifted blacks at 4–6%.
anti_patterns: Fake grain at uniform size and no halation
Heavy digital sharpening with film grain on top
Pushed saturation and a teal-orange split
Date stamps and borders over every frame
Hyper-sharp digital lenses with a film preset

composition.framing: Casual and honest; the frame holds a moment, not a layout.
composition.viewpoint: Eye height, handheld, 1 to 4m from the subject.
composition.geometry: Loose and natural; a horizon or a table edge shapes the frame.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre, with the face or object at a third and some of the surroundings left in.

principles.rule: Put the subject within 0.05 of 0.33 or 0.67 of the width.
Leave a margin of 5–15% and allow the frame to cut a hand or a plate.
Leave 30–50% of the frame as sky, wall or blur.
Use 2 to 3 planes at f/2.8: a soft foreground, a sharp subject and a blurred background.
Keep a scene range of 4 to 6 stops with lifted blacks at 4–6%.

light.quality: Natural and warm: sun, window or lamp, with a soft roll-off in highlights.
light.direction: Side or backlit by low sun, with flare allowed.

lens_and_camera.format: 35mm SLR or compact; digital with a film emulation as a hybrid
lens_and_camera.focus: Manual or zone focus; accept some missed frames.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Warm, soft colour with lifted blacks, creamy highlights and visible grain.
grade_recipe: Set the white balance at 5400K, tint +4.
Lift the black point to 5% and the white point to 96%.
Apply a soft S-curve with a gentle shoulder: highlights −15, shadows +15.
Shift greens toward yellow by −10 hue and drop blue saturation by −8%.
Add halation: red glow 6px, amount 20%, on highlights above 85%.
Add film grain, amount 35%, size 50%, roughness 55%.
colour_and_grade.grain: Portra 400: fine, even and organic at A4; Gold 200: tighter and warmer

subject_and_staging.staging: Light. Choose the place and the light; let the moment happen, and shoot 1 roll per outing.
subject_and_staging.direction: Do not ask for poses; ask people to carry on and shoot 3 frames in a row.

workflow: Send the roll to a lab and scan at 4000 dpi.
Correct dust and dirt by hand, and keep 90% of the grain.
Grade only in a global warm curve; avoid local brightening.
Add light leaks only where they were real.
post_processing.output: A warm, grainy file at 4:5 or 3:2, for feeds, books or small prints.

emotion.target_response: Nostalgia and warmth: the viewer feels a moment from their own life.

use_cases: image prompts for a warm analogue look
avoid_when: The brief needs product accuracy or exact colour.
The image must stay clean for small screens or print at high resolution.

modifiers.how: Use a 6×7 or 35mm slide film at ISO 100, f/8 and a tripod; keep warm light and saturated colour but drop the halation and the lift.
Add a direct on-camera flash at 1/16 power, an ISO 800 film and a blown-out ground; keep the grain.
